authority_impersonation: Police, prosecutors and courts in Vietnam never ask citizens to transfer money by phone or chat. Summons are delivered in writing.
There is no such thing as a 'temporary custody account' for an investigation. Verify in person at the local station or call 113.
Real officers do not demand secrecy from your family.
Traffic fines, utility arrears and social-insurance updates are paid through official portals (Cổng dịch vụ công, the provider's own app), never to a personal account.
safe_account: Banks never move your money to a 'safe account'. If someone asks you to do this, it is a scam.
Call the number printed on the back of your card, not a number the caller gave you.
investment_ponzi: A guaranteed 1% per day compounds to over 3,600% per year. No legitimate investment pays that.
'Tasks' that pay commissions and then require a deposit to withdraw are a documented scam pattern.
otp_request: Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN or password. Sharing an OTP hands over your account.
prize: You cannot win a lottery you did not enter. Paying a fee to receive a prize is the scam itself.
romance: Someone you have never met in person asking for money is the defining pattern of romance scams.
customs_fee: Customs and couriers do not collect fees through personal bank accounts.
reported_account: This account number appears on a public scam warning list. Money sent to reported accounts is rarely recovered.
generic: Pause. Verify through an official channel you look up yourself, not a number the other side gave you.
refund_scam: Refunds never require you to pay a fee first. A real refund goes back to the card or account you paid with.
relative_emergency: A relative or boss who 'changed number' and needs money urgently to a stranger's account is the deepfake script. Call the number you already have for them.
fake_receipt: A transfer receipt screenshot is not money. Check your own banking app; never pay a 'release' or 'activation' fee to receive a payment.
